improvements_suggested: Repair the milestone-scoped timing detector: when git-commit attribution returns 0, fall back to a results/ mtime scan bounded by the ops/changelog activation window, so the retro stops false-zeroing on milestones whose artifacts exist on disk.

Stamp duration_s plus a compute_bound flag onto every experiment artifact at write time, so slowest_experiments and compute_bound_experiments_count are computed from ground-truth artifacts rather than from commit attribution.

Emit detector_gap_suspected=true whenever artifacts for the active milestone exist on disk but the detector reports 0 commits, so the false-zero self-flags instead of being re-diagnosed by hand each milestone.
Tag aggregation/capstone milestones in the retro pipeline so a low compute-bound count reads as expected-for-aggregation rather than anomalous.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix the milestone-scoped timing detector (mtime + changelog-window fallback) -- the single recurring operational defect from .363 through .402, and the only thing blocking accurate efficiency retros.
Stamp duration_s + compute_bound on artifacts at emit time so slowest_experiments and compute_bound_experiments_count populate from ground truth.
Self-flag the gap (detector_gap_suspected) when on-disk artifacts contradict a 0-commit attribution, eliminating the per-milestone manual re-diagnosis.
meta_reflection: The milestone executed cleanly end-to-end (capstone exp4357 paper_ready=true, unmet_gates=[]); the only operational defect is the now-chronic false-zero timing detector, which has recurred .363->.402 without a code fix. Re-documenting the gap each milestone is itself wasted effort -- the highest-value move is to land the detector fix so future retros measure real per-experiment timing instead of re-deriving 'the artifacts are on disk' by hand.
